source_refs.note: Exercise 9.2, Question 2 (book p. 272); the book prints no answers for Exercise 9.2; answers checked with sympy and the solution book

blocks.explanation:
A difference of two \(\cos^{-1}\) angles must equal a \(\cos^{-1}\).
Plan: use formula (iv) directly, after finding the two square roots.
steps:
Given: \(\cos^{-1}\frac{7}{25}\) and \(\cos^{-1}\frac{5}{13}\).
To prove: their difference is \(\cos^{-1}\frac{323}{325}\).
Method: both terms are already \(\cos^{-1}\), so use formula (iv): \(\cos^{-1}x - \cos^{-1}y = \cos^{-1}\left(xy + \sqrt{(1-x^{2})(1-y^{2})}\right)\) with \(x = \frac{7}{25}\), \(y = \frac{5}{13}\).

Check the condition
\[x = \tfrac{7}{25} = 0.28,\quad y = \tfrac{5}{13} \approx 0.385\]
Why: formula (iv) needs \(x \le y\). Then \(\cos^{-1}x \ge \cos^{-1}y\), so the difference is not negative, as a \(\cos^{-1}\) value must be.

Find the square roots
\[\sqrt{1-x^{2}} = \sqrt{1 - \tfrac{49}{625}} = \tfrac{24}{25}\]
\[\sqrt{1-y^{2}} = \sqrt{1 - \tfrac{25}{169}} = \tfrac{12}{13}\]
Why: \(\frac{576}{625}\) and \(\frac{144}{169}\) are perfect squares (triples 7, 24, 25 and 5, 12, 13).

Apply formula (iv)
\[\text{L.H.S} = \cos^{-1}\left(\tfrac{7}{25}\cdot\tfrac{5}{13} + \tfrac{24}{25}\cdot\tfrac{12}{13}\right)\]
\[= \cos^{-1}\left(\tfrac{35}{325} + \tfrac{288}{325}\right)\]
\[= \cos^{-1}\tfrac{323}{325} = \text{R.H.S}\]
Why: for a difference the cosine formula has a plus sign. \(25 \times 13 = 325\), \(7 \times 5 = 35\), \(24 \times 12 = 288\), \(35 + 288 = 323\).

Check
\[\cos^{-1}0.28 - \cos^{-1}0.3846 \approx 1.2870 - 1.1760\]
\[= 0.1110\]
\[\cos^{-1}\tfrac{323}{325} \approx 0.1110\ \checkmark\]
Why: both sides give the same small angle (about \(6.4^{\circ}\)).
